newsitem.title: USA: Union Carbide Q2 helped by prices, costs.
newsitem.headline: Union Carbide Q2 helped by prices, costs.

text.p: Union Carbide Corp said Monday that improved pricing for polyethylene and ethylene glycol, and lower raw material costs compared to the first quarter, accounted for most of its second quarter gains.
Union Carbide reported earnings of $2.54 per primary share, compared to $2.34 the previous second quarter.
Sales rose to $1.666 billion for the quarter, compared to $1.559 billion for the comparable period in 1996.

The company said that a combination of volume increases and control of fixed costs resulted in fixed cost productivity improvement of 7.0 percent for the first half of 1997 compared to the 1996 first half, as measured by fixed cost per pound of product sold.
Union Carbide repurchased more than 1.8 million of its common shares during the second quarter at a cost of $87.1 million.
